<description>
Currently, multipath descriptor strings treat the multipath specifiers as syntactic sugar. Once we finish parsing such a string, the multipath elements are lost as the result is the multiple distinct descriptors that the multipath is a shorthand for. This means that we are unable to return the multipath string for such descriptors.

This PR allows descriptors to actually be multipath where the multipath specifiers are represented inside of the paths of `BIP32PubkeyProvider`s. This allows for the multipath string to be produced.

In order to achieve this, a lot of derivation path parsing is refactored. `KeyPath` is promoted to being its own class (which subclasses `std::vector`), while the individual derivation indexes become a `KeyPathElement` object so that the multipath elements can be represented. Furthermore, hardened derivation characters are now being stored within `KeyPathElement`s so each element knows what the original hardened character was. This also cleans up a little bit of the descriptor implementation as we no longer have to carry around `bool apostrophe` in a bunch of places.

Lastly, `Parse` now returns a single `Descriptor` object, rather than a vector of them. If the descriptor is a multipath descriptor, the expansion can be retrieved using `GetMultipathExpansion()`. The wallet uses this and still must not store multipath descriptors.
</description>

[2026-11-11] r:5853031703 review COMMENTED by fametrano (contributor):
The `migratewallet` fix holds on 0f2dc37a8bb5a5c668ebc8ab8f2d43d3f07c810d, but the PR adds no test for it.

achow101 fixed `SingleKeyPathElement::Unserialize` after my inline note on 74915efa. When I migrate a v29.4 legacy watch-only wallet that holds `wpkh([d34db33f/84h/0h/0h/0/5]<pubkey>)`, 0f2dc37a keeps the origin path `84h/0h/0h/0/5`, as v31.1 does; 74915efa gave `84h/0h/0h/0h/5h`. On 74915efa `bip32_tests` and `descriptor_tests` still pass. The test below reads a `KeyOriginInfo` back from its serialization: it fails on 74915efa (`2147483648 != 0`) and passes on 0f2dc37a.

```diff
--- a/src/test/bip32_tests.cpp
+++ b/src/test/bip32_tests.cpp
@@ -7,6 +7,7 @@
 #include <clientversion.h>
 #include <key.h>
 #include <key_io.h>
+#include <script/keyorigin.h>
 #include <streams.h>
 #include <test/util/common.h>
 #include <test/util/setup_common.h>
@@ -480,4 +481,21 @@ BOOST_AUTO_TEST_CASE(parse_hd_keypath)
     }
 }

+BOOST_AUTO_TEST_CASE(key_origin_serialization_roundtrip)
+{
+    // A key origin as the wallet stores it: unhardened steps stay unhardened when read back.
+    const auto path{ParseHDKeypath("m/84h/0h/0h/0/5")};
+    BOOST_REQUIRE(path);
+    KeyOriginInfo info{};
+    info.path = *path;
+    DataStream ss{};
+    ss << info;
+    KeyOriginInfo read;
+    ss >> read;
+    BOOST_REQUIRE_EQUAL(read.path.size(), path->size());
+    for (size_t i{0}; i < read.path.size(); ++i) {
+        BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL(read.path[i].ChildNumber(), path->at(i).ChildNumber());
+    }
+}
+
 BOOST_AUTO_TEST_SUITE_END()
```

The script that builds the wallet, the commands and their output are in https://gist.github.com/fametrano/fc7fd1b054657138a96a73befa81da66/5dabccf7307d47f9f2063df62fb7ce93e54ca0ab.
